commit.message:
go: update btcwallet for sync-time reorgs

During synchronization, wallet transactions may be recorded ahead of
its sync tip. Ignoring a matching block disconnect can leave old history
in place when a replacement block arrives.

Update btcwallet and wtxmgr together to the merged fixes in btcwallet
PRs #1403 and #1404. The store enforces one block identity per height;
the wallet reconciles orphaned and canonical history atomically,
preserving canonical coinbase spend chains and notifying clients only
of real spentness changes after commit.

Both modules use upstream commit 16cfb4483d1f. The range from our prior
pin contains only these two fixes and their regression tests. No schema
migration is required; existing inconsistent history is not repaired.

commit.message:
lnd: warn about an anchor commit fee cap below the floor

max-commit-fee-rate-anchors is set in whole sat/vbyte, so its lowest
accepted value, 1 sat/vbyte, converts to 250 sat/kw. That's below
chainfee.FeePerKwFloor, which now takes precedence over a lower cap
both when opening a channel and when updating its fee. So the setting
isn't honored as configured.

Log a warning at startup when that's the case, and say in the
description of the option that the minimum is used instead.

commit.message:
htlcswitch: never propose a commit fee rate below the floor

The link chooses the commitment fee rate of an update_fee with
IdealCommitFeeRate, which falls back to the min relay fee from the fee
estimator when the rate it would choose otherwise is lower. That relay
fee can be below chainfee.FeePerKwFloor: the bitcoind and btcd
estimators cap the median feefilter of our peers at the fee estimate
for the next block, even if that's below our own min relay fee, and the
web API estimator reports zero until its first successful fetch. The
link then proposed a fee rate that SignNextCommitment refused to sign,
as validateCommitmentSanity rejects it, and the link failed.

The relay fee also decides whether an increase of less than 10% is
worth an update_fee: only a channel whose fee rate is below the relay
fee gets one. So a channel already below the floor, such as one we
opened with an older lnd and max-commit-fee-rate-anchors=1, stayed
there while the relay fee was this low.

Use the floor as the min relay fee if the estimator reports a lower
one. As IdealCommitFeeRate falls back to the min relay fee, this also
covers a max-commit-fee-rate-anchors below the floor.

commit.message:
funding: never propose a commit fee rate below the floor

As the initiator, we propose our fee estimate for a confirmation target
of three blocks as the commitment fee rate, capped at
MaxAnchorsCommitFeeRate for anchor channels. The lowest accepted value
of max-commit-fee-rate-anchors, 1 sat/vbyte, converts to 250 sat/kw,
which is below chainfee.FeePerKwFloor. With that setting, we proposed
anchor channels at a rate below the floor.

Raise the proposed rate to the floor after applying the cap, so the
floor takes precedence over a lower cap. It also covers a fee estimate
below the floor.

commitment fee rate is below the minimum we accept. Since it's a
ReservationError, the funding manager sends its message to the peer
that proposed the channel.

commit.message:
funding: use a realistic anchor commit fee cap in tests

The funding manager test fixture didn't set MaxAnchorsCommitFeeRate, so
it was zero. The initiator caps the commitment fee rate of anchor
channels at that value, so every anchor and taproot channel opened in
these tests proposed a commitment fee rate of zero, which the channel
state machine rejects for every later commitment.

Set the cap to the default of max-commit-fee-rate-anchors, 10 sat/vbyte,
and carry it over when Alice's funding manager is recreated.
